html:
The United States has signed a landmark nuclear cooperation deal with Saudi Arabia, an agreement approved by Trump that could allow the Kingdom a path to enriching its own fuel for civilian reactors and is expected to last decades and be worth billions of dollars. This development signals a significant shift in regional alliances and global energy politics, even as a House Democrat calls for congressional hearings on the deal.

Middle East Conflict: Tensions continue to escalate across the Middle East as Yemen’s Houthis claim fresh attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, following their announced "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia. These claims are condemned by Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Bahrain, and Syria, while shipping data indicates more vessels are changing course. Concurrently, the US has launched more strikes on Iran, marking the twelfth consecutive night of attacks aimed at degrading Tehran’s ability to threaten ships in the Strait of Hormuz, deploying a B-1 bomber for the first time in the current escalation. In retaliation, Iran's Revolutionary Guard announced it stopped three oil tankers from passing through the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran’s Army drones hit US bases in Jordan and Bahrain, inflicting heavy damage and reportedly causing casualties among US forces. Trump has threatened to bomb and destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every ship Iran attacks in the Strait, prompting Iran to warn of a ‘powerful’ response if nuclear sites are attacked and promising similar retaliation. The war with Iran has already cost $37.5 billion, with the US seeking billions more from Congress.

Russia-Ukraine: Ukraine has appointed a new army chief, Mykhailo Drapatyi, following a week of nationwide protests over military strategy in the ongoing war with Russia. While Drapatyi's appointment was welcomed, many expressed a desire for the return of former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov. On the economic front, Russia's businesses are reportedly under strain from Ukrainian drone attacks on warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer. Meanwhile, Russia is also noted to be recruiting men from the world’s poorest countries to fight in Ukraine.

Global Economy: Google is reportedly burning through cash due to spiralling AI costs, with the company having projected spending as much as $190 billion on AI investments earlier this year. Trade tensions are also evident as Canada's 'powerful' dairy sector finds itself in Trump's trade crosshairs, singled out as an irritant justifying new tariffs. The Middle East conflict and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are exacerbating Europe’s gas crisis, while a Dubai firm has cut a deal for a new port to bypass the critical waterway. India is investing billions to build a domestic semiconductor industry, seeking to diversify global supply chains beyond Taiwan.

Climate & Health: Human-caused climate change has intensified Europe's risk of drought, with extreme heat becoming the primary driver of dry conditions, leading to wildfires ravaging Spain, France, and Italy and killing three firefighters. France recorded at least 5,700 more deaths than usual during a historic June heat wave. In Africa, camels, known as "ships of the desert," are suffering from rising temperatures. Separately, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has crossed a devastating threshold, with over 1,000 lives lost.

Other Developments: In Mexico, a mayor was killed in his town hall just months after surviving an assassination attempt. In India, police cracked down on 'cockroach' protesters who later used reels and memes to document their experiences and continue their message. Moroccan army officers have toured Gaza in preparation for a multinational force that will enter the area, even as Palestinian activists launch a campaign challenging the 'ceasefire' narrative and the death toll from Israeli aggression on Gaza rises to 73,305.
